business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P4 (10-Q MD&A)
business_model.claim: Guardian sells technology-enabled pharmacy services—including drug dispensing, compliance packaging, clinical coordination, caregiver training, and mock audits—to residents of long-term care facilities (LTCFs).
quotes: We are a leading, highly differentiated pharmacy services company that provides an extensive suite of technology-enabled services designed to help residents of LTCFs adhere to their appropriate drug regimen, which in turn helps reduce the cost of care and improve clinical outcomes.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K) and reiterated in P4 (10-Q)
business_model.claim: More than two-thirds of annual revenue is generated from residents of assisted living facilities (ALFs) and behavioral health facilities (BHFs); the remainder comes primarily from skilled nursing facilities (SNFs).
quotes: More than two-thirds of our annual revenue for each of the past three years has been generated from residents of ALFs and BHFs, which are our target markets, while the remainder has been generated primarily from residents of skilled nursing facilities ("SNFs").

business_model.claim: As of September 30, 2026, the company operated 63 pharmacies (57 full-service), serving approximately 218,000 residents in approximately 8,600 LTCFs across 39 states.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, our 63 pharmacies, 57 of which are full-service, served approximately 218,000 residents in approximately 8,600 LTCFs across 39 states.

business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by the number of residents served, prescriptions dispensed, drug price inflation, and acquisitions; in Q3 2026 residents grew from 204,000 to 218,000 and prescriptions from 7.3 million to 8.1 million year-over-year.
quotes: the number of residents served increased from 204,000 residents during September 2025 to 218,000 residents during September 2026 and prescriptions dispensed increased from 7.3 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025 to 8.1 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026.

business_model.claim: The Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) drug price negotiations, effective January 2026, reduced revenue per prescription; excluding acquisitions, organic Q3 2026 revenue fell $13.7 million year-over-year primarily due to IRA pricing decreases.
quotes: Excluding the $7.3 million increase in revenue attributable to the Acquisitions, organic revenue decreased by $13.7 million, primarily attributable to pricing decreases as a result of the IRA.

business_model.basis: stated in P4 (10-Q MD&A); percentage from P4 table
business_model.claim: Cost of goods sold consists primarily of prescription drug acquisition costs, pharmacy personnel expenses (salaries and benefits), delivery charges, and supporting overhead (rent, depreciation, amortization).
quotes: Cost of goods sold consists primarily of expenses associated with the fulfillment and delivery of the prescription, including prescription drug acquisition costs. Cost of goods sold also includes associated pharmacy personnel-related expenses, including salaries and benefits, delivery charges and other supporting overhead costs (such as rent and depreciation and amortization of assets used in the fulfillment and delivery of the prescription).

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A) and P4 (10-Q MD&A)
business_model.claim: Selling, general, and administrative expenses consist primarily of personnel-related costs (share-based compensation, salaries, benefits), facilities, software, insurance, professional services, and amortization of intangible assets.
quotes: Selling, general, and administrative expenses consist primarily of personnel-related expenses, including share-based compensation, salaries and benefits, for our employees at the pharmacies and support services engaged in other pharmacy related activities including sales and marketing, finance, legal, human resources, purchasing and other administrative functions.

business_model.claim: The company's core growth strategy combines organic growth (new LTCF relationships, increased resident adoption) with acquired growth (purchasing operating pharmacy businesses).
quotes: Our core growth strategy focuses on increasing the number of residents we serve through a combination of organic and acquired growth.

business_model.claim: The company operates a locally-managed pharmacy model with centralized corporate support, where each pharmacy is run by a President overseeing three directors, and centralized functions include data analytics, IT, financial oversight, purchasing, and regulatory support.
quotes: We believe that our business model promoting local management autonomy, combined with our centralized corporate support, results in superior service to LTCFs and their residents.

business_model.basis: stated in F1 (balance sheet) and P6 (earnings release)
business_model.claim: As of September 30, 2026, the company held $119,655 thousand in cash and cash equivalents with no long-term debt outstanding under its credit facility.
quotes: no long-term debt outstanding under our credit facility

business_model.claim: The company completed a follow-on offering in March 2026 of 1,020,000 shares at $31.00 per share, using all net proceeds to repurchase and retire an equal number of Class A shares issued upon Class B conversion, resulting in no change to total shares outstanding.
quotes: In March 2026, the Company completed an underwritten follow-on public offering (the "Q1 2026 Offering") of 1,020,000 shares of Class A common stock at an offering price of $31.00 per share.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K Business section and 10-Q MD&A as management's characterization of its market position.
competitive_position.claim: Guardian positions itself as a purpose-built, technology-enabled pharmacy services company focused on assisted living facilities (ALFs) and behavioral health facilities (BHFs), a segment where national competitors have primarily focused on skilled nursing facilities.
quotes: We are a leading, highly differentiated pharmacy services company that provides an extensive suite of technology-enabled services designed to help residents of LTCFs adhere to their appropriate drug regimen

While our national competitors have primarily focused on skilled nursing facilities ("SNFs"), we believe we enjoy a strong competitive position as a large and purpose-built provider of pharmacy services to ALFs and BHFs.

Net Income of $19.1 million, compared to $9.6 million in the prior-year period.

competitive_position.claim: During 2026, Guardian completed multiple acquisitions including Wellness Concepts (Virginia), Nautilus (14-state mail-order ALF pharmacy), and Van's Institutional Pharmacy (Tennessee and Kentucky), and added greenfield pharmacies in Lexington, Kentucky, Houston, and Huntsville.
quotes: In July, Guardian completed the acquisition of Wellness Concepts, a long-term care pharmacy serving Virginia's Shenandoah Valley region.

Guardian also completed the acquisition of certain assets of Nautilus, a pharmacy services provider that previously served assisted living communities across 14 states through a centralized mail-order model.
Earlier this week, Guardian completed the acquisition of Van's Institutional Pharmacy, a well-established long-term care pharmacy serving communities across western Tennessee and Kentucky.

the Lock-Up Holders have agreed not to offer, sell, distribute or otherwise dispose of or transfer any of the approximately 29.9 million shares of Class A common stock that are subject to those agreements, without the prior consent of the Company, during the period from the date of the agreement through September 14, 2027.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K Risk Factors as a risk to profitability and market share.
competitive_position.claim: Guardian faces intense competition from national, regional, and local institutional and retail pharmacies, some of which have greater financial resources and more established market presence.
quotes: The business of providing pharmacy services to LTCF residents is highly competitive, and we face competition from multiple sources. There are national, regional and local institutional pharmacies, as well as numerous local retail pharmacies, that provide pharmaceutical dispensing services comparable to those that we offer.
Some of our larger competitors have indicated that they plan to focus more on the ALF market, which could further increase the competition we face.

competitive_position.claim: State 'freedom of choice' laws allow LTCF residents to select their own pharmacy provider, preventing facilities from mandating Guardian as the exclusive supplier and increasing competitive pressure for resident adoption.
quotes: Certain states have a "freedom of choice" requirement as part of their state Medicaid programs or in separate legislation that enable a resident to select his or her provider. These laws may prevent LTCFs from requiring their residents to purchase pharmacy services or pharmaceuticals from particular providers that have a supplier relationship with the LTCF.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A as a factor affecting comparability of results.
competitive_position.claim: The Inflation Reduction Act's Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program took effect in January 2026 for the initial ten Part D drugs, reducing Guardian's revenue and cost of goods sold and is expected to continue impacting year-over-year comparability throughout 2026.
quotes: In January 2026, the initial ten Part D drugs that were part of IRA negotiations had their negotiated prices go into effect. The reduction in prices to the IRA-impacted drugs affects the comparability of results, specifically for revenue and cost of goods sold, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, which include the impact of the IRA, when compared against the results of the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, which do not include the impact of the IRA.
We expect IRA-related price reductions to continue impacting year-over-year comparability throughout the remainder of 2026.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Guardian's Q3 2026 revenue declined 1.7% year-over-year to $371.1 million, with organic revenue down $13.7 million primarily due to IRA pricing decreases, despite a 7% increase in residents served.
quotes: Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 decreased by $6.4 million or 1.7% compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. Excluding the $7.3 million increase in revenue attributable to the Acquisitions, organic revenue decreased by $13.7 million, primarily attributable to pricing decreases as a result of the IRA.
Reported Revenue of $371.1 million, inclusive of pricing decreases as a result of the IRA, down 2% year-over-year.

competitive_position.claim: Guardian's business is highly dependent on a small number of senior management personnel and its ability to attract and retain pharmacists and pharmacy professionals in a competitive labor market.
quotes: Our business is managed by a small number of senior management personnel, the loss of which could cause our business to suffer and materially adversely affect our operating results.

Competition for qualified pharmacists and other pharmacy professionals is intense. The loss of pharmacy personnel or the inability to attract or retain sufficient numbers of qualified pharmacy professionals could materially adversely affect our business.

competitive_position.claim: Guardian faces inflationary pressure on labor costs, supply costs, and transportation, which it states it generally cannot fully offset through pricing.
quotes: We are currently experiencing inflationary pressures on our operating costs. Among other things, competition for labor is becoming more acute and we expect our labor costs to increase as a result.

In addition, we have experienced increased costs for supplies, and rising fuel costs have resulted in increased costs for the transportation of drugs. We generally are not able to sufficiently raise our pricing to offset these increased costs.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K Risk Factors describing contract terms.
competitive_position.claim: Guardian's contracts with SNFs (1–3 years, 60-day termination notice) and ALF/BHF preferred-provider agreements (1–3 years, 30-day termination notice) can be terminated by either party, creating revenue concentration and relationship risk.
quotes: Our agreements with SNFs generally range from one to three years in duration and typically renew automatically for subsequent renewal terms. The SNF contracts can be terminated by either party generally upon 60 days' notice.
These contracts can be terminated by either party generally upon 30 days' notice.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 and P6 (resident and prescription counts, YoY growth); demographic rationale stated in P1 and P4
growth_thesis.claim: Organic growth in residents served and prescriptions dispensed is the primary volume driver: residents rose from 204,000 to 218,000 and Q3 prescriptions from 7.3 million to 8.1 million year-over-year; for this to continue, the ALF/BHF resident population must keep growing with aging demographics and Guardian must sustain rising resident-adoption rates in existing facilities.
quotes: the number of residents served increased from 204,000 residents during September 2025 to 218,000 residents during September 2026 and prescriptions dispensed increased from 7.3 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025 to 8.1 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026.
Residents served ended the quarter at approximately 218,000, up 7% year-over-year.

LTCF industry trends, including aging demographics, increases in the number of assisted living residents, improving life expectancies and enhanced quality of care, have resulted in ALF and BHF resident populations that require assistance with their increasingly acute and complex healthcare needs.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P6 (specific acquisitions named and completed) and P4 (dollar contribution to revenue)
growth_thesis.claim: Acquisition of existing pharmacy businesses adds residents and revenue immediately: in 2026 Guardian completed acquisitions of Wellness Concepts, Nautilus assets, a Sioux City pharmacy, and Van's Institutional Pharmacy, contributing $7.3 million to Q3 revenue; for this driver to persist, suitable institutional-pharmacy targets must remain available at prices that accrete to earnings and integration must proceed without disrupting existing resident relationships.
quotes: In July, Guardian completed the acquisition of Wellness Concepts, a long-term care pharmacy serving Virginia's Shenandoah Valley region.
Earlier this week, Guardian completed the acquisition of Van's Institutional Pharmacy, a well-established long-term care pharmacy serving communities across western Tennessee and Kentucky.
Excluding the $7.3 million increase in revenue attributable to the Acquisitions, organic revenue decreased by $13.7 million, primarily attributable to pricing decreases as a result of the IRA.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 and P3 (pharmacy counts by date); P6 names specific greenfield locations and their status
growth_thesis.claim: Greenfield pharmacy development expands the network footprint: the company grew from 61 pharmacies at year-end 2025 to 63 by September 2026, with the Lexington, Kentucky pharmacy now operational and new locations planned in Houston and Huntsville; for this to continue, demand must exist in each new market, staff must be recruited and trained, and each pharmacy must reach productive resident volume.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, our 63 pharmacies, 57 of which are full-service, served approximately 218,000 residents in approximately 8,600 LTCFs across 39 states.

Guardian also made progress on its greenfield development initiatives. Its previously announced pharmacy in Lexington, Kentucky is now operational. We are also advancing plans to expand our presence in Texas and Alabama, with new locations in Houston and Huntsville, respectively.
As of December 31, 2025, our 61 pharmacies, 54 of which are full-service, served approximately 205,000 residents in approximately 8,400 LTCFs across 38 states.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 (margin figures in table) and P6 (CEO commentary and guidance); the scalability claim is management's stated view
growth_thesis.claim: Operating leverage is expanding margins: Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 9.1% from 7.2% a year earlier, and Adjusted EBITDA grew 24% year-over-year to $33.9 million despite a 2% revenue decline; for this to continue, resident and prescription volume growth must outpace the growth in variable and fixed operating costs, and automation must keep reducing labor cost per prescription.
quotes: Adjusted EBITDA of $33.9 million, up 24% year-over-year.
Our margin improvement demonstrates the scalability of Guardian's operating model, as well as the progress we are making in driving profitability and leverage across our growing resident base.
Reported Revenue of $371.1 million, inclusive of pricing decreases as a result of the IRA, down 2% year-over-year.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 (machine count, platform names, described capabilities); competitive risk stated in P2
growth_thesis.claim: Proprietary technology and automation differentiate Guardian and underpin its efficiency model: the company deploys over 100 automated dispensing machines and operates proprietary platforms (Guardian Compass, GuardianShield) across its network; for this advantage to persist, continued capital investment in technology is required and competitors must not match or exceed these capabilities at lower cost.
quotes: we currently have over 100 automated dispensing machines deployed across our network.

Our centralized corporate support capabilities empower our local pharmacy operators to offer an extensive suite of high-touch, individualized, consultative pharmacy services, using a portfolio of proprietary data analytics systems and technology designed to help ensure that the right dose of the right medication is provided to the right resident at the right time.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 (IRA impact on revenue, forward-looking statement on continued impact) and P6 (CEO attributes revenue decline to IRA)
growth_thesis.claim: Inflation Reduction Act drug-price negotiations are a material revenue headwind that must be offset by volume growth: Q3 2026 revenue fell 2% year-over-year and organic revenue declined $13.7 million in the quarter, while the company expects IRA-related price reductions to continue impacting comparability throughout 2026; for growth to continue, per-prescription price declines must remain smaller than the revenue gained from additional residents and prescriptions.
quotes: We expect IRA-related price reductions to continue impacting year-over-year comparability throughout the remainder of 2026.
Excluding the $7.3 million increase in revenue attributable to the Acquisitions, organic revenue decreased by $13.7 million, primarily attributable to pricing decreases as a result of the IRA.
In January 2026, the initial ten Part D drugs that were part of IRA negotiations had their negotiated prices go into effect.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factors); the company's own language frames this as an unresolved uncertainty
growth_thesis.claim: Competitive intensity and resident freedom-of-choice laws constrain Guardian's ability to retain and grow its resident base: larger competitors are targeting the ALF segment, and state freedom-of-choice provisions allow residents to select any pharmacy; for growth to continue, Guardian's service quality, technology, and local relationships must be sufficient to retain residents against competing offers.
quotes: Some of our larger competitors have indicated that they plan to focus more on the ALF market, which could further increase the competition we face.
Certain states have a "freedom of choice" requirement as part of their state Medicaid programs or in separate legislation that enable a resident to select his or her provider.

The ability of a resident to select the pharmacy that supplies him or her with prescription drugs could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations because there can be no assurance that such resident will select us as a provider.

With a history spanning more than 50 years, Van's brings a strong reputation for quality care and service. The acquisition increases Guardian's Tennessee footprint to five pharmacy locations.

material_events.basis: stated in P6 (8-K earnings release, FY 2026 Outlook section)
material_events.claim: Guardian raised its full-year 2026 guidance, increasing revenue guidance to $1.44 billion–$1.46 billion (from $1.43 billion–$1.45 billion) and Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $136 million–$138 million (from $129 million–$131 million).
quotes: Updated Guidance | Previous Guidance / Revenue | $1.44 billion -$1.46 billion | $1.43 billion - $1.45 billion / Adjusted EBITDA | $136 million - $138 million | $129 million - $131 million

material_events.basis: stated in P4 (10-Q Part I Item 2 MD&A, Factors Affecting Comparability – Inflation Reduction Act section)
material_events.claim: The initial ten Part D drugs subject to IRA Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program had their negotiated prices go into effect, affecting Guardian's revenue and cost of goods sold comparability.
quotes: In January 2026, the initial ten Part D drugs that were part of IRA negotiations had their negotiated prices go into effect. The reduction in prices to the IRA-impacted drugs affects the comparability of results, specifically for revenue and cost of goods sold, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026

risks.basis: Stated directly in P4 (MD&A) and P6 (earnings release); F2 confirms the revenue decline in the income statement.
risks.claim: IRA-driven drug price reductions are eroding Guardian's revenue per prescription, causing organic revenue to decline even as resident and prescription volumes grow, and the company expects this impact to continue throughout 2026.
quotes: organic revenue decreased by $13.7 million, primarily attributable to pricing decreases as a result of the IRA
We expect IRA-related price reductions to continue impacting year-over-year comparability throughout the remainder of 2026.
Absent the price reductions from the IRA, revenues would have been up high single digits compared to the third quarter of 2025, mostly driven by organic growth

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors) and P1 (10-K Business section); growth figures from P3 and P4.
risks.claim: Larger competitors are shifting focus into the ALF and BHF segment where Guardian derives more than two-thirds of revenue, and state 'freedom of choice' laws allow residents to switch pharmacy providers, creating competitive pressure on Guardian's core market.
quotes: Some of our larger competitors have indicated that they plan to focus more on the ALF market, which could further increase the competition we face.
Certain states have a "freedom of choice" requirement as part of their state Medicaid programs or in separate legislation that enable a resident to select his or her provider.
More than two-thirds of our annual revenue for each of the past three years has been generated from residents of ALFs and BHFs, which are our target markets

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors); financial resilience from F1, F2, F3, P6.
risks.claim: Changes to Medicare, Medicaid, or private payor reimbursement rates, or adoption of a national average acquisition cost benchmark, could materially reduce Guardian's revenue and profitability.
quotes: Any changes that lower reimbursement rates under Medicare, Medicaid or private payor programs could result in a substantial reduction in our revenues.
CMS and other governmental agencies have advocated for the creation of a national average acquisition cost benchmark, which states may use to set pharmacy payment rates.
Given the significant competition in the industry, we have limited bargaining power to counter health plan payor demands for reduced reimbursement rates.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors); scale from P4.
risks.claim: Guardian's ALF and BHF preferred-provider agreements can be terminated by either party on 30 days' notice and do not guarantee the right to serve individual residents, creating exposure to sudden loss of facility relationships.
quotes: These contracts can be terminated by either party generally upon 30 days' notice.

the ALF and BHF contract does not automatically grant us the right to serve those residents. Instead, our sales team must market our pharmacy services to the individual residents in that community, each of whom has the right to choose their pharmacy provider.
There can be no assurance that these parties will not terminate all or a portion of their contracts with us.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors); margin improvement from P4 and F2.
risks.claim: Guardian faces inflationary pressure on labor and supply costs that it states it generally cannot pass through to customers via pricing, threatening margin expansion.
quotes: We are currently experiencing inflationary pressures on our operating costs.
We generally are not able to sufficiently raise our pricing to offset these increased costs.

Because labor costs are and will continue to be a major component of our operating expenses, higher labor costs, whether as a result of increased wages or increased staffing levels, could reduce our profitability and gross margins.
